Our stored knowledge has very little on this, and I don't want to guess at identifiers.

**What the file shows**

| Item | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Ravenscar** | Internal system | Toil & Trouble's consumer-complaint ticketing system. The client can search it on request. |
| **PressureMate TT-6200** | Product name and model number | The six-quart electric pressure cooker. Expect "TT-6200" in file names, tickets and test records. |
| **Lot designations (e.g., "Q3-2024 lot")** | Production-lot convention | This is how our notes refer to lots. The client's own lot-code format isn't recorded, so confirm it. |
| **"Lid hard to open"** | Complaint wording | Three complaints used this phrasing on other 2024 lots. Expect similar ticket categories or tags in Ravenscar. |
| **Rennick Odell** | Person | The technical contact. He may appear as an author or custodian. |

**What the file does not show**
- No Bates prefixes, document-control numbers, or file-naming conventions from earlier matters.
- No project or product code names.
- No other internal systems, such as engineering change, QA, test-lab, or document-management platforms.
- No identifiers for the independent laboratory lid testing the client says was done before launch. We have no lab name or report numbers.

**How to fill the gaps**
1. Check the firm's closed-matter files from earlier Toil & Trouble work, including the Okafor matter, for prior productions, privilege logs, and discovery responses. These are the most reliable source for Bates prefixes and system names.
2. Ask Mr. Oyelaran, with a copy to Delphine Moorcroft, for a short list of the relevant systems, lot-code formats, and any internal code names. Odell and other employees must be reached only through the client, not directly.
3. When the production arrives, ask the client for a data map or custodian list as part of the scope discussion.

Ravenscar and the complaint history shouldn't be raised with anyone outside the client or the firm until a request is served and scope is discussed. This list is for internal use only.
